answer_text:
Let \(\mathbb D\) be the unit disc. For \(a\in\mathbb D\), define the Blaschke factor

\[
b_a(z)=\frac{a-z}{1-\overline a z}.
\]

This is a Möbius automorphism of \(\mathbb D\), with \(b_a(a)=0\), and satisfies \(|b_a(z)|<1\) for \(|z|<1\).

If \(f:\mathbb D\to\mathbb D\) is analytic and \(f(a)=0\), then the Schwarz–Pick lemma gives

\[
|f(z)|
=
\left|\frac{f(z)-f(a)}{1-\overline{f(a)}f(z)}\right|
\le
\left|\frac{z-a}{1-\overline a z}\right|
=
|b_a(z)|.
\]

Apply this first with \(a=i/2\):

\[
|f(z)|\le |b_{i/2}(z)|.
\]

Set

\[
g(z)=\frac{f(z)}{b_{i/2}(z)}.
\]

The possible singularity at \(z=i/2\) is removable, and the inequality above shows \(|g(z)|\le 1\), so \(g:\mathbb D\to\mathbb D\). Also,

\[
g(-i/2)=\frac{f(-i/2)}{b_{i/2}(-i/2)}=0.
\]

Now apply Schwarz–Pick to \(g\) with \(a=-i/2\):

\[
|g(z)|\le |b_{-i/2}(z)|.
\]

Therefore

\[
|f(z)|
\le
|b_{i/2}(z)|\,|b_{-i/2}(z)|.
\]

Now evaluate at \(z=\frac12\):

\[
|b_{i/2}(1/2)|
=
\left|\frac{i/2-1/2}{1+i/4}\right|
=
\frac{\sqrt2/2}{\sqrt{17}/4}
=
\frac{2\sqrt2}{\sqrt{17}},
\]

and similarly,

\[
|b_{-i/2}(1/2)|
=
\frac{2\sqrt2}{\sqrt{17}}.
\]

Thus

\[
|f(1/2)|
\le
\left(\frac{2\sqrt2}{\sqrt{17}}\right)^2
=
\frac{8}{17}.
\]

This upper bound is attained by the finite Blaschke product with exactly those zeros:

\[
f_0(z)=b_{i/2}(z)b_{-i/2}(z)
=
\frac{(i/2-z)(-i/2-z)}{(1+iz/2)(1-iz/2)}
=
\frac{1+4z^2}{4+z^2}.
\]

Indeed,

\[
f_0(1/2)=\frac{1+4(1/4)}{4+1/4}
=
\frac{2}{17/4}
=
\frac{8}{17}.
\]

Therefore the largest possible value is

\[
\boxed{\frac{8}{17}},
\]

attained, for example, by

\[
\boxed{f(z)=\frac{1+4z^2}{4+z^2}}.
\]
